Honestly never make reviews but I adopted a cat from here and genuinely she was in such horrible shape I took her to the vet that day. She was very overweight, in a pretty small cage, ear mites in her ear, she had a respiratory infection that they did not inform me about, and her coat was greasy and dandruff due to her weight. Very disappointing considering this cat is so sweet (The cat is doing much better now).

I already emailed customer service. I guess they don’t respond unless a public complaint is made.

I have never found the employees at this Pet Supermarket to be particularly friendly. Despite shopping here occasionally to buy food for my feral cat colonies and rescue cats, I am rarely greeted when I walk into the store.  I have walked in many times and observed the employees gathered in conversations opposed to greeting customers.

On my most recent visit, a 32-pack of Friskies was displayed with a $19.99 price tag underneath it. When I checked out, it rang up at $26. I pointed out the discrepancy, and instead of addressing it right away, I was left waiting while other customers were checked out. There were two employees present, and it seemed that one could have assisted me while the other continued working the register. Instead, I stood there waiting, unsure what was going to happen.

Eventually, the employee who rang me up brought up a 24-pack and took the 32-pack that was placed above the $19.99 “sale price” back. The employee matched the advertised “discounted” price for the smaller pack, which is the same regular price big box retailers sell the same food. Obviously overpriced.. The whole situation seemed to be an inconvenience for the employees, so I ultimately said, "Never mind."

Then, I mentioned that the Pet Supermarket on Richmond, which recently closed, would have simply honored the displayed price. Jennifer responded, "We're not that store." My reply was, "No, you definitely are not."
I shop here to buy food for animals that depend on me, and good customer service still matters. Unfortunately, this store consistently feels indifferent toward its customers.

Pet Supermarket, you closed the wrong store.

The store manager, Eddie Wesley was incredibly rude.
I grabbed some treats for my pup from the sale rack.
I specifically grabbed a braided, a stick and a rounded chewable.
The braid and stick had 50% off tags on them individually. The rounded chewable was in a box of others like it and the box was labeled 50% off.
When Eddie was ringing me up, I noticed he didn’t take 50% off the rounded one and I told him I got it from a bin that was marked as 50%.
He then told me that because it did not have a sticker on it. It wasn’t 50% off. And so I told him OK sir well, I just want to let you know that you have it in a bin of others that are like it that is marked 50% off. Then he said you’re not listening to me look down look at the sticker and see that it doesn’t have 50% off on it. I said I understand that I just don’t think that you’re understanding me and I left the store.
I was really surprised that a manager was talking to a customer that way, I’ve been in that store several times and I’ve never seen that gentleman before however, I will not be bringing my business back to this location ever again.

I used to come here all the time to bathe my two dogs at the wash station for $10 each, which included the use of the tub, shampoo, conditioner, towel and the blow dryer. It was so accommodating and felt like they actually put the customer first. It was reasonable to bring both dogs, so I only ever bathed them there.

Now the prices for dog washes are tiered and the basic for $14.99 doesn’t even include access to the blow dryer. The blow dry option is 19.99! I’m not paying $30-$40, when it used to cost me $20 for both dogs. I just wash them at home for free now.

I was a loyal customer for years, but I won’t be coming back unless the dog wash prices go back down. It reeks of corporate greed. I also stopped buying their brand food, Performatrin Ultra, after this because I won’t be supporting a company that takes advantage of their customers.
Great place

I recently visited Pet Supermarket, and unfortunately, I had a very disappointing experience with an older associate named Marty. I was using the middle bowl area to wash my dog and was preparing to move over to the dryer after the previous customer left. However, Marty told me I couldn’t move to the dryer because there was a bigger dog in the area, despite the fact that I was there first and the dog was actually medium-sized—not large.

It felt really unfair, especially since there was plenty of space to accommodate both dogs, and I was told to move when I shouldn’t have had to. To make matters worse, moving the dryer was difficult, as it was positioned too high for me to adjust easily.

I understand that situations arise, but the way this was handled made me feel like my concerns weren’t valued as a paying customer. It’s disappointing to see a lack of consideration and fairness. I’m seriously reconsidering returning to this location after this encounter. I hope the management will address how customers are treated, as we all deserve equal respect and service.
